items.question: There are 40 more buyers in the grocery store today than yesterday. There were half the number of buyers yesterday as there were the day before, and the day before had 50 buyers. Nobody visited the store on more than one day. What's the total number of buyers who've visited the store in the three days?

previous_f3_program: collection("grocery_store.daily_buyer_counts", "buyer_count", "grocery_store", source("buyers who've visited the store in the three days"))
member("grocery_store.daily_buyer_counts", at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "today"), source("buyers in the grocery store today"))
member("grocery_store.daily_buyer_counts", at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "yesterday"), source("buyers yesterday"))
member("grocery_store.daily_buyer_counts", at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "day_before"), source("the day before had 50 buyers"))
offset(at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "today"), at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "yesterday"), 40, "count", source("There are 40 more buyers in the grocery store today than yesterday"))
fraction_of(at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "yesterday"), at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "day_before"), 1, 2, source("There were half the number of buyers yesterday as there were the day before"))
observe(at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "day_before"), 50, "count", source("the day before had 50 buyers"))
partition("grocery_store.daily_buyer_counts", at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "three_days"), source("Nobody visited the store on more than one day"))
query("value", at("grocery_store.buyers.count", "three_days"))

items.question: A business executive is going on a four day vacation where he will be unable to answer emails.  The first day he is gone, he receives 16 new emails.  On each of the following days, he receives half as many new emails as he received on the prior day.  At the end of his four day vacation, how many new emails will he have received in total?

previous_f3_program: collection("business_executive.vacation.new_emails", "email", "business_executive", source("he receives 16 new emails"))
observe(at("business_executive.vacation.duration", "planned"), 4, "day", source("four day vacation"))
add("receive_day_1_emails", "business_executive", at("business_executive.vacation.new_emails.count", "current"), 16, source("The first day he is gone, he receives 16 new emails"))

add("receive_day_2_emails", "business_executive", at("business_executive.vacation.new_emails.count", "current"), fraction(event_field("receive_day_1_emails", "quantity"), 1, 2), source("On each of the following days, he receives half as many new emails as he received on the prior day"))

add("receive_day_3_emails", "business_executive", at("business_executive.vacation.new_emails.count", "current"), fraction(event_field("receive_day_2_emails", "quantity"), 1, 2), source("On each of the following days, he receives half as many new emails as he received on the prior day"))

add("receive_day_4_emails", "business_executive", at("business_executive.vacation.new_emails.count", "current"), fraction(event_field("receive_day_3_emails", "quantity"), 1, 2), source("On each of the following days, he receives half as many new emails as he received on the prior day"))
query("sum", "business_executive.vacation.new_emails", "end_of_four_day_vacation")

items.question: Bert has a garden shop. He buys his products in a warehouse and sells them for $10 more in his shop. From each sale, he has to pay 10% of the value in tax. One day a client came to his shop and bought a barrel for $90. How Much money did Bert make on this sale?

previous_f3_program: transfer("buy_products", "bert", "warehouse.products", "bert.products", "bert.products.purchased.count", source("He buys his products in a warehouse"))
offset(at("bert.products.barrel.sale_price", "sale_day"), at("bert.products.barrel.warehouse_purchase_price", "purchase_day"), 10, "currency", source("sells them for $10 more in his shop"))
percent_of(at("bert.products.barrel.sale_tax", "sale_day"), at("bert.products.barrel.sale_price", "sale_day"), 10, source("From each sale, he has to pay 10% of the value in tax"))
transfer("sell_barrel", "client", "bert.products.barrels", "client.products.barrels", 1, source("a client came to his shop and bought a barrel for $90"))
observe(at("bert.products.barrel.sale_price", "sale_day"), 90, "currency", source("bought a barrel for $90"))
query("value", at("bert.products.barrel.money_made", "sale_day"))

items.question: Emma's bank account has $100 in it. Each day of the week, she spends $8. At the end of the week, she goes to the bank and asks for as many $5 bills as her account can give her. She leaves the rest in the account. How many dollars remain in the account?

Angeli had 90 assorted candies. One-third of the candies were lollipops and the rest were candy canes. She then shared the lollipops equally among the boys such that each boy received 3. She then shared the candy canes equally among the girls such that each received 2. How many boys and girls were given altogether?

previous_f3_program: collection("angeli.candies", "candy", "angeli", source("Angeli had 90 assorted candies"))
observe(at("angeli.candies.count", "initial"), 90, "count", source("Angeli had 90 assorted candies"))
member("angeli.candies", "angeli.candies.lollipops", source("One-third of the candies were lollipops"))
member("angeli.candies", "angeli.candies.candy_canes", source("the rest were candy canes"))
partition("angeli.candies", at("angeli.candies.count", "initial"), source("One-third of the candies were lollipops and the rest were candy canes"))
fraction_of(at("angeli.candies.lollipops.count", "initial"), at("angeli.candies.count", "initial"), 1, 3, source("One-third of the candies were lollipops"))
collection("angeli.candy_recipient_groups", "recipient_group", "angeli.candy_sharing", source("the boys such that each boy received 3. She then shared the candy canes equally among the girls"))
member("angeli.candy_recipient_groups", "angeli.candy_recipient_groups.boys", source("the boys"))
member("angeli.candy_recipient_groups", "angeli.candy_recipient_groups.girls", source("the girls"))

transfer("share_lollipops", "angeli", at("angeli.candies.lollipops.count", "current"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.boys.lollipops.count", "current"), at("angeli.candies.lollipops.count", "initial"), source("She then shared the lollipops equally among the boys"))
observe(at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.boys.lollipops_per_person.count", "after_sharing"), 3, "count", source("each boy received 3"))

product_relation(event_field("share_lollipops", "quantity"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.boys.count", "after_sharing"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.boys.lollipops_per_person.count", "after_sharing"), source("shared the lollipops equally among the boys such that each boy received 3"))

transfer("share_candy_canes", "angeli", at("angeli.candies.candy_canes.count", "current"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.girls.candy_canes.count", "current"), at("angeli.candies.candy_canes.count", "initial"), source("She then shared the candy canes equally among the girls"))
observe(at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.girls.candy_canes_per_person.count", "after_sharing"), 2, "count", source("each received 2"))

product_relation(event_field("share_candy_canes", "quantity"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.girls.count", "after_sharing"), at("angeli.candy_recipient_groups.girls.candy_canes_per_person.count", "after_sharing"), source("shared the candy canes equally among the girls such that each received 2"))
query("sum", "angeli.candy_recipient_groups", "after_sharing")
